Activity.description:
One connected agent. Lives exactly as long as its wrapper's connection to
the daemon; nothing here is persisted.
What an agent's row says it is doing right now (see CONTEXT.md: Activity).

text.description: One bounded line. The producer bounds it; consumers render it whole.

ActivityKind.description:
Which of its two kinds an Activity is. The ranking between them is the
producer's job — a consumer only ever styles them.

oneOf.description: The harness's own account of its current step ("Reading 1 file…").

The submitted ask the current Turn is working on — never text still
being typed.

activity.description:
What the agent is doing, in words. Never a phrase amon composed — a
label amon wrote itself would say no more than the state column already
does (ADR-0017, ADR-0020).

Absent for an agent whose harness amon cannot yet read, and for one
whose screen cannot be believed right now.

agent.description:
Agent kind, e.g. `claude`. Free-form so that a wrapper built against a
newer agent list still registers against an older daemon.

agent_session_id.description: Reported by integration hooks; absent when none are installed.

args.description: Argv of the wrapped agent, agent name included.

branch.description:
The git branch [`AgentEntry::cwd`] is on, when it is on one.

Absent outside a repository, and absent on a detached HEAD — which has
a commit but no branch. Read from `.git/HEAD` rather than by running
git, so a directory git would understand and this does not reads as
absent too: a blank column rather than a wrong one.

focused.description:
Whether the agent's terminal *view* has input focus. Absent until a
focus signal arrives; a focused window can host many views, so this is
finer-grained than the compositor's notion of focus.

id.description:
Generated by the wrapper at launch. Also handed to integration hooks as
`AMON_AGENT_ID`.

pid.description: Process id of the wrapped agent, not of the wrapper.

project.description:
The Project [`AgentEntry::cwd`] belongs to: the repository it is in,
named by its root directory. A linked worktree's Project is the
repository it was cut from, not the worktree's own directory — a
worktree's path names neither its project nor its branch.

Absent outside a repository, where the directory itself identifies the
agent and a consumer shows that instead.

runtime.description:
Set when this agent lives inside an agent runtime (herdr, luvus)
rather than under an amon wrapper.

seen.description:
Whether the terminal view has had focus since the current
[`AgentEntry::state`] began. `Idle` and not seen is "finished but
unnoticed" — an annotation on the state rather than a state of its own,
which is why [`AgentEntry::attention`] exists: to combine the two in one
place instead of leaving every consumer to invent the same rule.

state_since.description: When the agent last entered [`AgentEntry::state`], unix milliseconds.

subpath.description:
Where inside its checkout the agent sits, relative to the checkout
root. Absent at the root, which is the ordinary case, and absent
wherever [`AgentEntry::project`] is. Relative to the *worktree* for an
agent in one, because the repository does not contain that path.

window.description:
The compositor window hosting the agent's terminal, as an opaque
compositor-native token. Absent off a supported compositor, or when the
wrapper could not identify its window unambiguously — never guessed.
Consumers hand it back to the compositor rather than parsing it.

workspace.description: Display name of the workspace holding [`AgentEntry::window`].

AgentPatch.description:
A partial update to an entry. Absent fields are left alone, which is what
lets an old wrapper omit fields a newer daemon knows about.

activity.description:
Two levels deep, like [`AgentPatch::window`]: a session that ended took
its activity with it, and the row has to be able to say so rather than
keep narrating the session before it.

branch.description:
Two levels deep, like [`AgentPatch::window`]: checking out a detached
HEAD has to be expressible as "no longer on a branch" rather than
leaving the old name standing.

cwd.description:
Where the agent is working now. An agent can change directory — into a
worktree, into a sibling checkout — and takes its Project and its
branch with it, so all four move together or none of them do.

project.description:
Two levels deep, like the branch below: an agent that walks out of a
repository has to be able to say so rather than keep naming the last
one it was in.

window.description:
Two levels deep because "no longer known" has to be expressible:
absent means leave alone, `null` means clear, a string means set. A
window that closed has to be able to say so rather than be left stale.

AgentState.description:
The state of a wrapped agent, as arbitrated by its wrapper.

These are herdr's detection states; amon does not add to them.

oneOf.description: Finished, prompt visible, nothing happening.
Actively working.
Needs human input.
Running, but not recognized as an agent.

BarConfig.description: What the workspace indicators draw, and how fast.

frame_ms.description: How long one spinner frame is shown, in milliseconds.

marker_beats.description: Beats spent showing the focus marker.

state_beats.description:
Beats of the focused workspace's turn-taking spent showing the agent's
state. A beat is half a turn of the spinner (ADR-0008).

Config.description: The whole of the user's configuration.

oneOf.description: The frame was not a JSON object with an `id` and a `method`.
A method this peer does not implement — including one from a newer amon.
No registry entry with that id.

Event.description:
Pushed by the daemon to every subscriber, unsolicited.

[`Event::Unknown`] is what makes a subscriber built against an older amon
survive a newer daemon: events it has never heard of land here and are
skipped rather than breaking the stream.

oneOf.description: An agent registered.
An agent's entry changed — state, window, or session identity.
An agent's wrapper disconnected; its entry is gone.

The config file changed and has been re-read (ADR-0012). Carries the
whole configuration rather than a diff: it is small, it is read rarely,
and a subscriber that applies a whole answer cannot drift from one that
missed an earlier event.

A release newer than the running daemon exists. Broadcast when a
check finds one, and replayed to every later subscriber — a panel
restarted after the check must not wait a day to hear about it.
Versions are bare (`0.2.0`), never tagged (`v0.2.0`).

GlyphConfig.description:
Which character stands for each condition.

Plain characters, never markup: this chooses *which* glyph, never how it is
drawn. A workspace at rest keeps the underline the widget computes for
itself, and nothing here can reach it.

focused.description: The marker for the workspace you are on.

working.description:
The animation frames for a working agent, in order. Any length; one
frame is a static glyph that happens to be redrawn.

version.description: Version of the amon binary on the connecting side.

ReportActivity.description:
A hook reporting an Activity. amon-only: herdr has no counterpart, because
herdr collects state, not content (ADR-0021 — a seam, not a modified
vendored asset). A `prompt` opens a Turn with the exact submitted text; a
`narration` is the harness's own account of its current step, for agents
whose screens amon cannot read. The wrapper bounds the text.

ReportSession.description:
A hook reporting session identity. Mirrors herdr's
`pane.report_agent_session`.

ReportState.description:
A hook reporting agent state. Field names mirror herdr's `pane.report_agent`
so that vendored hook assets need only mechanical renaming.

seq.description: Monotonic per-source sequence number, used to drop out-of-order reports.

oneOf.description: Opens any connection to the daemon.

Wrapper claims a registry entry. The entry lives until this connection
drops.
Wrapper reports a change to its own entry.
Lists connected agents.
The user's configuration, as the daemon last read it (ADR-0012).
Turns this connection into an event stream.
Asks an older daemon to exit so a newer binary can take over.
Hook → wrapper.
Hook → wrapper.
Hook → wrapper. amon-only (ADR-0021).

Role.description:
What a peer is, declared in its [`Hello`].

Declarative, not load-bearing: what a connection can do is decided by the
methods it sends (`agent.register` claims an entry, `subscribe` starts the
event stream), so the daemon does not branch on this. It exists for
diagnostics and for future daemons that may want to.

oneOf.description:
An installed integration hook, talking to a wrapper rather than the
daemon. Hooks do not actually send a hello — they send one request and
hang up — but the role exists so their frames can be described.

Runtime.description:
Where a runtime-hosted agent lives. Present exactly on entries a runtime
module of the daemon projects; wrapped agents never carry it.

One variant per runtime, tagged by `kind`, so a consumer that only badges
or filters reads one field and each runtime keeps its own address shape.
What a variant carries is what the focus hop needs — the socket travels
with the entry so the CLI does not re-derive the runtime's path rules.

pane.description:
The pane hosting the agent (`w1:p1`) — what `agent.focus` takes.
Pane ids change when panes move across herdr workspaces, so the
daemon refreshes this and consumers must not cache it.

session.description: Session name; absent for the default session.

socket.description: Absolute path of the session's JSON API socket.

pane.description:
The pane hosting the agent — what `pane.focus` takes. luvus pane
ids are stable for the pane's life.

session.description: Session name; absent for the default session.

socket.description: Absolute path of the session's UHP socket.

SoundConfig.description: When to make a noise, and which one.

blocked.description: Played when an agent starts waiting for a human.

done.description:
Played when an agent finishes without being watched. Absent means the
bundled sound; a relative path resolves from the config file's own
directory, the way herdr's does.

enabled.description:
On unless turned off.

This started as off-by-default, reasoning that a tool which begins
making noise on upgrade is a tool people turn off entirely. The counter
is stronger: the whole point is to tell you about an agent you are *not*
watching, and a notification nobody knows exists notifies nobody. The
two sounds are rare — an agent finishing unwatched, or starting to wait
for you — and the config file `amon setup` writes shows how to silence
them.

UpdatesConfig.description: Whether the daemon may look for newer releases.

check.description:
On unless turned off. The whole of the check is one HEAD request
against the release page's stable redirect, at most daily; nothing
about this machine travels with it.

description:
The whole protocol in one document, so that non-Rust peers — the installed
integration hooks are shell and JavaScript — have something to validate
against.
title: Protocol
